servo: shorten interface availablility timeout Change the timeout to 5 seconds instead of one minute, so servod isn't unusable for such a long time. If someone accidentally tries to access a cr50 control while servod is disconnected, servod shouldn't become unusable for one minute. 5 seconds should be long enough. The servod wait is just supposed to wait for a device that quickly recovers not a device that is permanently disconnected. Also the watchdog dies before 60 seconds. By the time servod stops waiting the watchdog would have killed it, so 60 seconds is way too long. shill: metrics: Rename WiFiStatusType to WiFiReasonType The WiFiStatusType enum is used exclusively for representing the type of wifi disconnect reason. Since the standard uses "reason" to mean a disconnect reason and "status" to mean an auth/assoc status code, it makes sense to be consistent and use "reason" in this case. This change also fixes a bug in which kStatusCodeMax was used instead of kReasonCodeMax for the maximum value of a disconnect reason code (which likely occurred in the first place because the code did not consistently use "reason" when appropriate). shill: wifi: Use supplicant disconnect reason code for metrics Prior to this change, the metrics for disconnect reason codes did not come from supplicant, but instead were parsed from netlink messages. Not only was this an unnecessary duplication of functionality, but it meant that WiFi code and the corresponding disconnect metric were not necessarily in sync. This change modifies the situation such that this metric is updated by disconnect reasons received from supplicant. The primary functional difference this change makes is to stop converting kReasonCodeReserved* disconnect reasons into kReasonCodeInvalid, as the previous behavior made it more difficult to understand the actual distribution of disconnect reasons, without providing much benefit (also, kReasonCodeInvalid is the maximum value of a uint16_t, and so is outside the range of the reason code enum to begin with). BUG=None TEST=-All unit tests are passing. -Manual testing with extra logging added in Metrics::Notify80211Disconnect. CHROMIUM: bluetooth: Enable filter duplicates field for passive scan This sets the filter duplicates field in LE Set Scan Enabled command to enabled for passive scanning. By enabling the field, the advertisement reports from the same address would be sent to the host once per passive scan cycle. However, since the buffer to keep the seen address is limited (e.g. the size of buffer is 50 for Intel controllers), the host will still be interrupted by any advertisement report with new addresses beyond the size of the buffer. And the filtering duplicates was applied to at least 50 addresses in Bluetooth-noisy environment. vm_tools: concierge: fix reporting of disk usage Crostini VM disks can be sparse files, which means that their actual storage usage on the host filesystem (like 'du') may be less than their logical size (like 'ls'). This difference was accounted for by using stat(2), but that code path was lost when support for plugin VMs was added to ListVmDisks. This change restores the stat-based calculation of disk space usage for single-file disk images, like Crostini disks, resulting in more accurate reporting of free disk space for Linux storage in the Storage Management page in settings. It does not modify the calculation used for directory-based images (plugin VMs), so they will continue to over-report disk usage if those disks are sparse files.
